{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Strongly convex-strongly concave saddle points: exact joint gradients and squared distance.\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{CV\_\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}SCSC}



Minimax optimization



Solve \AtlasInlineMath{\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)}, with \AtlasInlineMath{z=(x,y)}.



\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present; Bounds missing



\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Strongly convex strongly concave saddle; solution concept: Joint squared distance; task family: Minimax



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Strong concavity in the declared block; convexity: Strong convexity in the declared block; convexity: Strongly convex strongly concave; initialization: Initial distance; smoothness: Lipschitz gradient



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Exact joint gradient; operation: Payoff joint gradient; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; query domain: Full space; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function first derivative



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic algorithms; restriction: Explicitly no additional algorithm restrictions; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Primal dual pair; postprocessing: Measurable postprocessing; postprocessing: Unqueried output explicitly allowed



\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Squared distance

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N grad; precision: Bit precision not counted



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Solve \AtlasInlineMath{\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)}, with \AtlasInlineMath{z=(x,y)}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The spaces are \AtlasInlineMath{X=\mathbb R^{d_x}} and \AtlasInlineMath{Y=\mathbb R^{d_y}}.



The function \AtlasInlineMath{f} is jointly \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}-smooth, uniformly \AtlasInlineMath{\mu_x}-strongly convex in \AtlasInlineMath{x}, and uniformly \AtlasInlineMath{\mu_y}-strongly concave in \AtlasInlineMath{y}; \AtlasInlineMath{\beta\ge\max\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}>0}.



A unique saddle point \AtlasInlineMath{z^\star} exists, and the public initial point satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


Public inputs include block dimensions \AtlasInlineMath{d_x,d_y} and \AtlasInlineMath{R^2}, \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}, \AtlasInlineMath{\mu_x}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\mu_y}, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.




\AtlasMath{z\in X\times Y\longmapsto \nabla f(z)}




Return the exact complete joint gradient, without function values or a Hessian.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return a feasible pair \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{z}=(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\in X\times Y}.



The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}



\AtlasMath{\|\widehat{z}-z^\star\|_2^2}




Do not use a global gap that may be infinite on an unbounded domain.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


Each joint-gradient response increments \AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm grad}} by one.



Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified \AtlasInlineMath{N} on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.



Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


Any measurable sequential adaptive deterministic algorithm is allowed. Queries and outputs may use the complete history, with no additional span, zero-support, communication, or memory restriction.



The same deterministic algorithm must satisfy the guarantee for every admissible instance.




\AtlasMath{\|\widehat{z}-z^\star\|_2^2\le\varepsilon.}




\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed worst-case query cap



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{R^2}: Public squared Euclidean distance bound from the initial point to the unique saddle point \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.



\AtlasInlineMath{\|z_0-z^\star\|_2^2\le R^2}



\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: Euclidean Lipschitz upper bound for the population payoff's complete joint gradient. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.



\AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le\beta\|z-w\|_2}



\AtlasInlineMath{d}: The joint Euclidean dimension is \AtlasInlineMath{d=d_x+d_y}. Within its stated window, the lower bound may choose finite block dimensions. \textbf{Domain:} Integer at least \AtlasInlineMath{2}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Squared Euclidean distance tolerance to the unique saddle point. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.



\AtlasInlineMath{\|\widehat z-z^\star\|_2^2\le\varepsilon}



\AtlasInlineMath{\mu}: Smaller curvature constant of the two variable blocks \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.



\AtlasInlineMath{\min\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}}



\AtlasInlineMath{\mu_x}: Uniform strong-convexity lower bound for \AtlasInlineMath{f(\cdot,y)} at every fixed \AtlasInlineMath{y} \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\mu_x\le\beta}.



\AtlasInlineMath{f(u,y)\ge f(x,y)+\langle\nabla_xf(x,y),u-x\rangle+\frac{\mu_x}{2}\|u-x\|_2^2}



\AtlasInlineMath{\mu_y}: A uniform strong-convexity lower bound for -f(x,·) at every fixed x; equivalently, the dual strong-concavity modulus of f. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\mu_y\le\beta}.



\AtlasInlineMath{f(x,v)\le f(x,y)+\langle\nabla_yf(x,y),v-y\rangle-\frac{\mu_y}{2}\|v-y\|_2^2}



\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms. \textbf{Domain:} The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.



\AtlasInlineMath{\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}}



\AtlasInlineMath{d_x,d_y}: Positive integer primal and dual block dimensions; joint dimension \AtlasInlineMath{d=d_x+d_y} \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{f}: Unknown real-valued payoff, with primal and dual input blocks. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{f:(x,y)\mapsto f(x,y)\in\mathbb R}.



\AtlasInlineMath{x,y,z}: Primal variable, dual variable, and joint point \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ y\in\mathbb R^{d_y},\ z=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{z=(x,y)}



\AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f,\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f}: Complete joint gradient and its two blocks \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla_x f\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ \nabla_y f\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f=(\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f)}



\AtlasInlineMath{X,Y}: Full space of the two unconstrained variable blocks \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{X\subset\mathbb R^{d_x},\ Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{X=\mathbb R^{d_x},\ Y=\mathbb R^{d_y}}



\AtlasInlineMath{z_0,z^\star}: Public initial point and the same solution appearing in the model assumption \textbf{Domain:} Feasible domain of this profile; the distance bound refers to the same solution.



\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x,\widehat y}: The point or variable blocks ultimately returned by the algorithm, corresponding to the hatted variables in the error formula. \textbf{Domain:} Feasible variable pairs in \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat z}: Joint output consisting of the two variable blocks \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat z=(\widehat x,\widehat y)}



\AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm grad}}: The number of complete exact joint-gradient calls. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.



\AtlasInlineMath{N}: A uniform cap on principal information calls for every admissible instance and execution path. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{N^\star}: The infimum principal query budget among algorithms satisfying every stated instancewise output guarantee. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative extended real value; by convention, positive infinity if no successful algorithm or no uniform finite budget exists.



\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A,I}: An algorithm selected from public inputs and an admissible hidden instance fixed before interaction \textbf{Domain:} The specified algorithm and model classes.



\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde O}: Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching, and upper bounds hiding the stated logarithmic factors, within the corresponding regions. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative complexity function; subscript p permits additional dependence only on fixed p.



\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\ln,\log_+}: Natural logarithm and its nonnegative truncation \textbf{Domain:} Arguments of log and ln are positive; the argument of \AtlasInlineMath{\log_+} may be zero.



\AtlasInlineMath{\log_+(t)=\log(\max\{1,t\})}



\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Initial-distance radius, the nonnegative square root of parameter \AtlasInlineMath{R^2}. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative real.



\AtlasInlineMath{R=\sqrt{R^2}}



\AtlasInlineMath{F}: Saddle operator induced by the payoff function \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{X\times Y\to\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{F(x,y)=(\nabla_xf(x,y),-\nabla_yf(x,y))}



\AtlasInlineMath{\mathfrak A_\varepsilon}: Algorithms using the allowed interfaces, algorithm restrictions, and output domain, and satisfying the displayed complete error guarantee for every fixed admissible instance \textbf{Domain:} The algorithm class is defined at fixed public parameters and target tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}.
